Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Expectation2: Adhere to site protocols and work effectively as part of the team.
Situation2: The mandatory daily pre-work safety briefing is starting in two minutes.
Story: My phone buzzed violently on the nightstand, jolting me awake. It was 4:58 a.m. I saw my friend’s name on the screen, and when I answered, all I could hear was sobbing. Through broken words, she told me her father had just passed away. My heart twisted—I knew she needed me to listen, to be there, to help her hold the pieces together. But as I tried to comfort her, I glanced at the clock. The safety briefing at the construction site started in two minutes, and missing it meant not just a reprimand, but possibly being sent home for the day. My team counted on me to be there, to pull my weight and follow the rules. I could already picture my supervisor’s disappointed face, the letdown in my coworkers’ eyes. My friend’s voice trembled in my ear, desperate for support, while the weight of my hard hat in my hand reminded me of my other responsibility. I stood there, torn, the world pressing in from both sides, not knowing which role to let down.
